cleanup_inspection: DropManaged clears the local live flag before dispatching the exact dynamic_store drop helper.
Store drop snapshots ptr/len, writes len=0 before element teardown, visits prefix slots in ascending index and Managed fields in declaration order, then calls bytes.release exactly once.

Within allowed elements, ByteBuffer fields dispatch zil.bytes.drop and finite user resources dispatch their checked teardown; unsupported Store, owning-array State and closure elements cannot reach this loop.

Push commits a complete element to an initialized slot before increasing len; on full it returns the original owning Package as error payload. Pop reduces len before loading the returned element, so stale tail memory has no obligation.
The ordinary 166/170 error cleanup continues through packages::teardown_paths, so allowed returned push/pop Package fields and nested-170 error payloads keep the existing checked recursive cleanup.
Store causes allocator runtime declarations to be emitted even if no ByteBuffer definition exists. Store helper and existing byte runtime reserve names avoid silently replacing foreign ABI.

Independent Store inline layout matches LLVM enum/record/tuple/array/error representation conventions; reserve uses actual LLVM stride and rejects negative/overflow request before allocation or head mutation.
